cases.title: Bystander killed outside Soulard bar
cases.happened: Early on June 28, 2026, several scuffles broke out as a group left a bar in Soulard. According to the victim's aunt, a 20-year-old man was behind a car when shots were fired, and a bullet ricocheted off a sign and struck him, and he died.
cases.claim: Police identified a man as the shooter. Police told the aunt that the decision not to charge rested on a self-defense claim. The aunt says later video put the shooter in a parking lot more than 200 feet away, and she rejects the claim. A defense attorney not involved in the case said self-defense would be unusual at a significant distance, depending on the circumstances.
cases.ended: The Circuit Attorney's Office declined charges. It does not disclose its reasons, but said homicide cases can raise complex questions of self-defense and defense of others.
cases.note: Status as of Aug. 13, 2026. Much of this account comes from the victim's family, not from prosecutors. The shooter's own account has not been reported.

cases.area: Near Energizer Park, St. Louis City
cases.title: Shooting near stadium during City SC game
cases.happened: On June 28, 2026, a shooting happened near Energizer Park during a City SC game. Police arrested a 19-year-old man.
cases.claim: Sources told First Alert 4 that prosecutors declined first-degree assault, armed criminal action and weapon charges, citing self-defense. Details of the claim have not been reported.
cases.ended: The Circuit Attorney's Office disputed that report, saying the charging decision was still under consideration and the investigation was ongoing.
cases.note: Status as of Aug. 13, 2026. Very little has been reported, and the final decision is unconfirmed.

cases.area: Near Fairground Park, St. Louis City
cases.title: Rifle shooting at a cookout
cases.outcome: Murder: not guilty. Gun charge: guilty
cases.happened: On March 15, 2025, an argument broke out at a cookout after a 44-year-old man repeatedly asked Turley Smith, 32, why he was there. Authorities say Smith shot the man 17 times with a high-powered rifle, including once in the back while the man was on the ground.
cases.claim: Smith said the man pulled a pistol from his pants and racked the slide. He said he feared for his life, and he denied standing over the body and continuing to fire. The report doesn't say whether a pistol was recovered.
cases.ended: On April 22, 2026, a jury found Smith not guilty of first-degree murder and armed criminal action. It found him guilty of unlawful possession of a firearm because of a 2014 felony robbery conviction.
cases.note: Sentencing on the gun charge had not been set when this was reported. A self-defense verdict did not protect him from the separate gun charge.

cases.title: Fatal shooting in a domestic incident
cases.happened: Around 8:30 a.m. on Sept. 7, 2025, a 33-year-old man was shot on Abaco Drive in Ferguson and died at a hospital. The prosecutor said it appeared to be a domestic incident.
cases.claim: The prosecutor said a self-defense claim was being investigated. Details of the claim have not been reported.
cases.ended: The suspect was released because no charges were filed within the 24-hour holding limit. Police had applied for charges and were still consulting with the St. Louis County Prosecutor's Office.
cases.note: Status as of Sept. 8, 2025. I couldn't find a final charging decision.

cases.title: Father shot adult son at close range
cases.happened: On April 30, 2024, a 31-year-old man came home with an 11-year-old child and woke his father, Tekeia Henderson. The father became irritated with the child, and a physical confrontation followed when the son stepped in to protect the child. The father shot him twice at close range.
cases.claim: At trial, Henderson claimed self-defense and also said the shooting was an accident.
cases.ended: On June 13, 2025, a jury found Henderson guilty of first-degree murder and armed criminal action. The murder charge carries a mandatory life sentence without parole.
cases.note: Sentencing was set for July 18, 2025. I didn't confirm the final sentence.

cases.title: Fight between two women ended in a fatal shot
cases.happened: On March 3, 2024, two women were fighting on Thomas Street. Authorities say one, 28, drew a gun and shot the other, 26, in the thigh, and she died.
cases.claim: The shooter told police she acted in self-defense. Police said at the time that witnesses did not support that claim.
cases.ended: She was charged with first-degree murder and armed criminal action. A Post-Dispatch tracker entry links to a story headlined "St. Louis murder case dropped after woman claims self-defense."
cases.note: Unconfirmed. I couldn't open the full Post-Dispatch story, so the reason for dropping the case and the date are not verified. The date shown is my estimate. Her name is left out for that reason.

cases.area: Bates St, south St. Louis City
cases.title: Hammer confrontation in a house being remodeled
cases.happened: In 2019, Kevin Patrick was working on the second floor of a home he was remodeling when he heard a noise downstairs. He says he told the intruder twice to leave, then got his gun.
cases.claim: Patrick testified that the man grabbed a hammer and "raised it in a threatening manner." He shot the man several times and claimed protection under Missouri's castle doctrine.
cases.ended: Charges were dismissed, then refiled in February 2024 as involuntary manslaughter and armed criminal action. Patrick waived a jury and was tried in August 2024. Judge Christopher McGraugh found him not guilty, ruling the state had not proved beyond a reasonable doubt that he didn't act in self-defense. The man's blood and DNA were on the hammer.
cases.note: A coworker testified about seeing the man enter, but the judge found that testimony inconsistent with the coworker's own actions. The case took about five years to end.

cases.title: Homeowner shot burglar inside the home
cases.happened: Around 4 a.m. on May 14, 2024, a man entered a home on Empress Drive and tried to throw property out a window. Two residents were inside. Court documents say he had earlier tried to enter another home nearby.
cases.claim: The homeowner shot him once. No statement from the homeowner was reported. The man ran past officers, was tracked by a police dog, and was hospitalized in critical condition.
cases.ended: The man who broke in, 27, was charged with first-degree burglary, attempted burglary and resisting arrest. No charges were reported against the homeowner.
cases.note: No formal statement clearing the homeowner was found. This is based on no charges being reported.

cases.title: Man shot in the back and head
cases.happened: Around 10:20 a.m. on Feb. 17, 2024, police found a 38-year-old man shot in the back and head in the 900 block of N. Kingshighway. He died at a hospital.
cases.claim: Police said the Circuit Attorney's Office cited self-defense. What the shooter said, and what led to the shooting, were not reported.
cases.ended: A suspect was taken into custody, and the Circuit Attorney's Office refused charges.
cases.note: Very few details were released, so this one offers little to learn from beyond the outcome. Reports don't explain how wounds to the back fit the self-defense finding.

cases.title: Neighbor shot inside an apartment building
cases.happened: Just after 2 p.m. on a Friday in February 2024, a 42-year-old man was shot inside The Loft apartments on Olive Street. He died at a hospital.
cases.claim: A 29-year-old neighbor was arrested at the scene. Prosecutors said the shooting was "in self-defense." What led to it was not reported.
cases.ended: Police applied for charges, and prosecutors declined them.

cases.area: St. Louis Place, St. Louis City
cases.title: Gunfight with bar security killed a bystander
cases.outcome: Murder: not guilty. Other charges dismissed
cases.happened: In October 2021, Rodregus Fuqua was kicked out of a bar during a family celebration, and he and his brother were beaten. A gunfight followed in which a security guard, an off-duty police officer, fired at Fuqua and Fuqua fired back. A 52-year-old bystander was hit by a stray bullet and died months later. Fuqua was paralyzed.
cases.ended: A first trial ended in a mistrial after prosecutors disclosed key evidence midway through. At the second trial, the jury acquitted him of second-degree murder and deadlocked on assault and armed criminal action, and prosecutors then dismissed those charges.
cases.note: The River Front Times called it the third self-defense murder acquittal in the city in about a month. The article is undated, so the date shown is my estimate. It shows that a bystander's death can still lead to a murder charge.

cases.title: Road-rage shootout, motorbike rider and Jeep driver
cases.happened: On Aug. 26, 2022, Michael Henderson, 19, a rapper known as CTS Luh Wick, was on a motorbike near a Jeep. Video showed him riding beside the Jeep, speeding ahead, turning and firing. The 42-year-old driver was shot in the head and died. Henderson fled before police arrived.
cases.claim: Henderson testified that he clipped the Jeep in traffic and saw the driver pointing a gun at him: "I was just doing what I felt that I had to do to protect myself." His attorney said a gun with eight spent cartridges was found in the Jeep. Prosecutors argued he was playing a game of chicken and "was not scared in that moment."
cases.ended: After about two hours of deliberation in January 2024, a jury found him not guilty of first-degree murder and armed criminal action.
cases.note: Evidence that the other driver had a gun and may have fired appears central, even though Henderson left the scene.

cases.title: Two brothers shot during a domestic dispute
cases.happened: In November 2022, a woman called her twin sister saying her boyfriend was beating her. The sister went to the house with Austin Heflin and another man, and called 911. According to their statements, the boyfriend's brother arrived, broke a window and came in with a gun, and the brothers began beating the other man. The sister handed Heflin her gun, and he fired four times, killing both brothers.
cases.claim: Heflin's attorney argued the boyfriend was the initial aggressor and that deadly force was justified to defend himself or another person. Police had a different account, saying Heflin held the boyfriend down while the brother displayed a handgun. Court documents say the brother's gun was never fired. One brother was shot once in the back.
cases.ended: Charged first with murder, then manslaughter. In January 2024, days before trial, Circuit Attorney Gabe Gore dismissed the charges, saying the evidence supported only self-defense. He said he would refile only if new evidence emerged.
cases.note: The victims' family strongly objected. A judge had earlier sanctioned the prior administration for withholding 911 recordings and DNA evidence, and a key witness died before the first trial date.
